Case No.-238/2022 dated 30.05.2022 registered for offences under Sections 302, 120-B/34 of IPC and Section 25(1-B) A/26/27/35 of the Arms Act. The High Court dismissed the bail application.

issue.issue_text: Whether a Final Report/Chargesheet is compliant with Section 173(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, even if the investigation is kept open against other accused, or if it is filed without all the documents required under Section 173(5).

facts: The issue arises in situations where an investigating officer files a Final Report/Chargesheet against some accused persons while keeping the investigation open against others.
A similar issue arises when a chargesheet is filed without being accompanied by all the documents and statements required under Section 173(5) of the Cr.P.C.
In these scenarios, accused persons often argue that the chargesheet is incomplete or non-compliant with Section 173(2), and therefore, they are entitled to default bail under Section 167(2) Cr.P.C.
law: Section 173(2) of the Cr.P.C. mandates the police to forward a final report (chargesheet) to a Magistrate upon completion of an investigation.
A chargesheet is defined as the opinion of the investigating officer, based on collected material, that an offense appears to have been committed by a particular person or persons.
This report under Section 173(2) forms the basis for a competent court to take cognizance of an offense.
Section 173(5) of the Cr.P.C. requires the investigating officer to forward all relevant documents and statements along with the chargesheet.
Section 173(8) of the Cr.P.C. permits the police to conduct a "further investigation" even after a chargesheet has been filed.

The Court referenced its judgments in *Dinesh Dalmia v. CBI* and *CBI v. Kapil Wadhwan*, which held that a chargesheet is not vitiated (invalidated) merely because all documents are not filed with it or because further investigation is pending.
application: The Supreme Court reasoned that the fundamental purpose of a chargesheet is to enable the court to assess whether an offense has been committed and to take cognizance.

The Court held that if the material produced along with the chargesheet is sufficient for the court to be satisfied about the commission of an offense and to take cognizance against the accused, the chargesheet is valid.
The pendency of a "further investigation" under Section 173(8) against other accused does not render the chargesheet filed against the current accused incomplete or invalid.
Similarly, the non-availability of some documents at the time of filing the chargesheet does not vitiate the report itself.

The Court clarified that these factors—keeping the investigation open for others or not attaching all documents—do not invalidate the chargesheet and do not give the accused a right to claim default bail on the grounds that the chargesheet is incomplete.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that a Final Report/Chargesheet is compliant with Section 173(2) of the Cr.P.C. and is not vitiated, even if the investigation is kept open against other accused or if it is filed without all the documents required under Section 173(5). The chargesheet is considered valid as long as it contains sufficient material for the court to take cognizance of the offense against the accused named in it.

arguments.issue_text: Whether a Final Report/Chargesheet is compliant with Section 173(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, even if the investigation is kept open against other accused, or if it is filed without all the documents required under Section 173(5).
appellant_arguments: The appellant likely argued that a chargesheet filed while an investigation is still pending against other accused, or without all the necessary documents, is an 'incomplete chargesheet' and does not comply with Section 173(2) of the Cr.P.C., thereby entitling the accused to default bail.
respondent_arguments: The respondent likely argued that a chargesheet is complete and valid for the purpose of Section 173(2) if it contains sufficient material for the court to take cognizance of the offence against the accused. The pendency of further investigation against other accused under Section 173(8) or the non-production of some documents does not vitiate the chargesheet or create a right to default bail.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: Having regard to the provisions contained in Section 173, the report of a police officer on the completion of an investigation shall contain: (a) the names of the parties; (b) the nature of the information; and (d) whether any offence appears to have been committed and, if so, by whom.
